title: Approve the working preview in the browser, and reject it into rework
description:
SPIDR child 3 of task-f3edb8fb39ad42ce8980dae7d62b604c (architect-20a6d1eb, 2026-09-05). dependsOn child 1 (task-40e52fa8a85a4921b97bee933b00403f, the kind) and child 2 (task-f5a74c23f8754665ab9d36cba386e1d0, the receipt this UI renders). This is the PROOF row for the Gate 2 feature: it owns the browser journey, the live drive, the docs sweep and the adversarial pass, so neither sibling files its own evidence row (global rail 21).

WHAT THIS ROW OWNS: the operator's side of Gate 2. A Needs-you card 'Approve working preview' carrying the loopback URL (opening in a new tab), the captured screenshots inline, and Approve / Reject-with-findings. The goal status strip gains a PREVIEW stage. Runs shows the preview receipt per goal. REJECT moves the named nodes to REWORK on the board with the findings text visible.

MEASURED AT HEAD df5bbfd5 (branch moe/work-2026-09-04) by architect-20a6d1eb - every pattern this row needs already exists, so it composes rather than invents:
- The Needs-you card + offer-wire pattern: `apps/control-room/src/v2/approvals/needs-you.tsx` and `offer-wire.ts` (`spendOffer`), with `escalation-port.ts` as the closest working example of a human decision reaching the daemon.
- The browser-side roster a new decide kind touches, traced from `escalation.decide`: live/live-activity.ts, v2/approvals/needs-you-model.ts, v2/goals/goal-status.ts, v2/goals/work-labels.ts, v2/ops/activity-words.ts.
- The board's REWORK column already exists: `apps/control-room/src/v2/board/board-columns.ts:20` BOARD_COLUMNS includes REWORK, and :47 routes a READY node with prior review rounds there. Rejecting into rework should reuse that column, not add one.
- The Playwright lane: `pnpm test:e2e:browser` = `tsc -p tests/e2e/control-room/tsconfig.json && playwright test -c tests/e2e/control-room/playwright.config.ts`; existing specs under tests/e2e/control-room/ drive a REAL daemon (daemon-board.spec.ts, prd-to-approval.spec.ts).

WORDS ARE THE PRODUCT HERE. Gate 2's question to the human is 'Is this product good enough and visually correct?' - the card must ask that, not surface a receipt dump. Refusal words render verbatim from the daemon's codes.
definitionOfDone: The Needs-you card renders for a goal with a STARTED preview receipt: the loopback URL as a link opening in a new tab, the captured screenshots inline, and both Approve and Reject-with-findings controls. A control-room test asserts all three are present and that the card is ABSENT when no preview receipt exists.

APPROVE commits a durable decision that is read back from `/activity/read` carrying its verdict - assert the verdict value from the activity read, not from local component state, so a click that never reached the daemon cannot pass.

REJECT with findings RENDERS THE FINDINGS AGAINST THE NAMED NODE on the preview card and in the goal's activity words, and the node's board column does NOT change: the daemon records a PreviewDecisionRecord whose findings name nodes of the active graph (preview-daemon-edge.ts:68-78) and performs no node transition, and BOARD_COLUMNS stays exactly its six entries (board-columns.ts:17-19; a REWORK column is a design regression under rail 2). Assert: the rejected node shows the finding text, the card offers the operator the path back to work (the existing plan/re-run affordance, not a synthetic column), and the column read for that node is unchanged before and after the rejection.

The goal status strip shows a PREVIEW stage while a preview is running, and the four refusal codes render as operator words, verbatim from the daemon: PREVIEW_COMMAND_MISSING, PREVIEW_START_TIMEOUT, PREVIEW_GOAL_NOT_LANDED, PREVIEW_DECISION_INVALID. Assert the rendered sentence for at least PREVIEW_COMMAND_MISSING and PREVIEW_START_TIMEOUT, and that an unknown code still renders verbatim rather than blank.

A Playwright journey under tests/e2e/control-room/ against a REAL daemon covers start -> card -> approve, with the `pnpm test:e2e:browser` count line quoted. No fixture-backed substitute (parent rail 4).

LIVE DRIVE: a preview started for UnAI (D:/projexts/UnAI) or a fresh scaffold app, with a real screenshot (path + sha256) and the committed decision recorded in a row comment under ~4500 chars. README's 'no working preview' clause is rewritten to the measured truth; `git grep -n 'no working preview'` returns 0 hits. If the live drive did not happen, say so plainly rather than implying it did.
Gates quoted with their count lines: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`, `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test`, `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm test`, `pnpm test:e2e:browser`.
taskRails: THIS ROW PROVES, IT DOES NOT REBUILD. If the card cannot render because child 2's receipt is missing a member, comment on THAT row and report blocked on it - do not add a daemon field here (global rail 4: a proof that repairs its own subject retires the question unanswered).

REUSE THE EXISTING PATTERNS: offer-wire.ts `spendOffer` for the decision, the existing REWORK column for rejection, needs-you.tsx for the card. A second decision wire or a new board column is a design regression, not a feature.

WORDS FOR HUMANS, not for tests (memory ui-legibility-pass-landed-2026-09-04). Ask Gate 2's actual question. Avoid an aria-live region that re-announces on every poll - PR #26's review caught exactly that; announce once and keep counters outside the live region.
FEATURES ONLY (inherited): no security-boundary or policy work.

Check any new testid namespace is free before using it (`cr.board.*` was already taken once, memory board-screen-landed-2026-09-04), and keep JSX ASCII-only - an apostrophe in JSX reds the scheduler boundary scan.

implementationPlan.description:
MEASURE AND VERIFY THE LEAF. NO EDITS.

(a) **THE LEAF MUST BE LANDED.** `dependsOn` names task-4a6e7bdbef9a4344829a7ce49c6fb378. Confirm AT THE TREE: `grep -n "preview" apps/daemon/src/http/http-listener-read-dispatch.ts` must now show the receipt read route registered, and the capture route must serve bytes confined to `.moe-next/previews/<goalId>/<sha>/`. At planning that grep returned **ZERO** across ~25 read routes. **If it still does, STOP and `moe.report_blocked` naming the leaf.** Do not add a daemon route here, and **do not render the card from a fixture to make it look alive** — that is the substitute parent rail 4 forbids.

(b) **RECORD THE SERVED SHAPE** the leaf actually landed: the receipt read's exact keys and the capture route's URL form. Step 2's decoder must match it exactly, and guessing here produces a decoder that rejects everything.

(c) **CONFIRM THE DECISION PORT IS STILL DONE.** `preview-port.ts:72` returns `spendOffer(wire, PREVIEW_COMMAND_KIND, affordance, payload, "ui-preview", PREVIEW_LAYER)` (75 lines, six arms green, landed at 432217be). This row CONSUMES it. If you find yourself writing a second decision path, stop — rail 2 calls that a design regression and the port's own docblock at `:10` says one wire is shared with every inline decision.

(d) **FIND THE STATUS STRIP** that DoD 4 needs a PREVIEW stage on, and name the file and its stage roster in the step note. I deliberately did not guess its path — measure it rather than inheriting a wrong name from this plan.

(e) **RE-MEASURE THE FOUR TIGHT FILES**: `needs-you-model.ts` (226 at planning), `needs-you.tsx` (212), `activity-words.ts` (133), `preview-port.ts` (75). All under 250, none with much room. Note that THREE rows are extending `NEEDS_YOU_KINDS` (needs-you-model.ts:35) concurrently.

(f) **CONFIRM DoD 3'S PREMISE IS STILL FALSE**, so step 6 is acting on current fact: `grep -rn "REWORK" apps/control-room/src` and `git grep -n "REWORK" -- apps/daemon/src` (tests excluded). Both returned ZERO at planning, and `BOARD_COLUMNS` (board-columns.ts:17-19) is six entries with no REWORK. If a peer has since landed one, say so — that changes step 6 entirely.

(g) **BASELINE THE GATES**: `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test`, `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`, `pnpm typecheck`. Standalone and foreground, failing paths and count lines recorded. Do not queue a leased baseline if a fleet-shared BEFORE is citable — cite it with holder, task, timestamps, sha and count line, and disclose HEAD drift.

THE BROWSER READER. NEW `apps/control-room/src/live/live-preview.ts` plus its test — the client for the route the leaf landed.

Follow the existing `live/` readers exactly (`live-runs.ts` is the closest shape): POST the read, decode the answer with an **EXACT-KEY** decoder, return a typed view or `null`. An unknown key is REFUSED, not ignored — that is what stops the daemon widening the shape later without the browser noticing.

**DECODE WHAT THE LEAF SERVES, NOT WHAT THIS PLAN GUESSES.** Step 1(b) recorded the real shape. The receipt carries `url` (string|null), `screenshots[]` (each with `journeyRef` and `path`), `outcome` ("REFUSED"|"STARTED") and `code` (PreviewCode|null) — but match the served keys exactly.

**A GOAL WITH NO RECEIPT IS ABSENT, NOT AN ERROR.** DoD 1 requires the card to be ABSENT when no preview receipt exists, so the reader must distinguish "no receipt" from "the read failed". Those are different states and the card renders differently for each.

**BUILD THE SCREENSHOT URL FROM THE SERVED PATH**, using the capture route's form. Do NOT construct a filesystem path in the browser or interpolate a raw `path` into a URL without encoding — the leaf confines the route server-side, and the client must not hand it something that looks like an escape attempt.

Render nothing here. This module reads and decodes; the card is step 3.

THE CARD. `apps/control-room/src/v2/approvals/needs-you-model.ts` (226) and `needs-you.tsx` (212) — **both tight against the 250 cap; extract before growing either past it.**

**MODEL:** add the preview kind to `NEEDS_YOU_KINDS` (needs-you-model.ts:35) and the model entry that carries the receipt view from step 2. **THREE ROWS ARE EDITING THIS ROSTER CONCURRENTLY** (task-a988ca1c, task-84cd2e55, this one) — rebase around peer entries and **never delete one** to make a count line tidy.

**CARD (DoD 1), three things present when a STARTED receipt exists:**
- the loopback **URL as a link opening in a new tab**;
- the captured **screenshots inline**, via the capture route;
- **both Approve and Reject-with-findings controls**, spending the offer through the ALREADY-LANDED `preview-port.ts:72` (rail 2, risk C). Do not write a second decision wire.

**THE CARD IS ABSENT WHEN NO RECEIPT EXISTS** — absent, not a dead control. An operator seeing a disabled Approve button on a goal with no preview learns nothing; a card that is not there is honest.

**WORDS FOR HUMANS, ANNOUNCED ONCE** (rail 3, risk E): no aria-live region that re-announces on every poll — PR #26's review caught exactly that. Announce once and keep counters OUTSIDE the live region.

**ASCII-ONLY, NO APOSTROPHES IN JSX** (risk G) — write "cannot" rather than a contraction. Confirm the testid namespace is free before using it; `cr.board.*` was taken once already.

THE WORDS AND THE STAGE (DoD 4). `apps/control-room/src/v2/ops/activity-words.ts` (133) and the status strip step 1(d) identified. **`activity-words.test.ts` does not exist yet — this step creates it.**

**THE FOUR REFUSAL CODES RENDER AS OPERATOR WORDS, VERBATIM FROM THE DAEMON**: `PREVIEW_COMMAND_MISSING`, `PREVIEW_START_TIMEOUT`, `PREVIEW_GOAL_NOT_LANDED`, `PREVIEW_DECISION_INVALID`. Each sentence says what happened and what the operator can do about it — the code is shown ALONGSIDE the words, never instead of them. DoD 4 names `PREVIEW_COMMAND_MISSING` and `PREVIEW_START_TIMEOUT` as the two whose rendered sentence must be asserted.

**AN UNKNOWN CODE RENDERS VERBATIM, NEVER BLANK** (DoD 4, risk F). A word map that silently swallows an unrostered code leaves an operator staring at an empty card with no way to find out why. Fall through to the raw code rather than to nothing.

**THE STATUS STRIP SHOWS A PREVIEW STAGE WHILE A PREVIEW IS RUNNING** — driven by the receipt's `outcome`, not by local component state. `activity-words.ts` collides with two peer rows; keep the edit to the entries this row adds.

THE JOURNEY (DoD 5). NEW spec under `tests/e2e/control-room/` against a REAL daemon: **start -> card -> approve.**

**NO FIXTURE-BACKED SUBSTITUTE** (parent rail 4). The claim is that the operator does this in a browser against a real daemon; a fixture makes the test pass while proving nothing about the product.

**DoD 2 IS THE LOAD-BEARING ASSERTION AND IT IS NOT A UI CHECK.** After Approve, read the verdict back from **`/activity/read`** and assert its value there — **not from local component state**. A click that rendered optimistically and never reached the daemon must fail this. That is the whole point of the clause.

REUSE THE EXISTING HARNESS (`activation-fresh-project.spec.ts` stands up a real daemon and pairs the tab). **Note the pairing shape**: a paired tab is a session-ledger principal, not the operator principal — if a step refuses `OPERATOR_PRINCIPAL_REQUIRED`, that is an authorization fact to report, not a test bug to work around.

**CLEAN UP ON EVERY EXIT PATH INCLUDING FAILURES** (epic rail 4): the daemon, any preview process and any temp directory die in teardown, not in a trailing statement. A leaked preview server holds a port and makes every later gate on this board inadmissible.

**QUOTE THE SPEC COUNT AND NAME THE SPEC** (risk H): `test:e2e:browser` is `tsc && playwright test`, so a typecheck failure means zero specs ran and the exit code alone cannot tell you.

**DoD 3 — STOP HERE AND RECORD. DO NOT IMPLEMENT, DO NOT GUESS, DO NOT DROP IT.**

DoD 3 reads: *"REJECT with findings moves the named node to REWORK on the board... Assert the node's column is REWORK (reusing the existing BOARD_COLUMNS entry, board-columns.ts:20)."* **That clause is unsatisfiable as written**, measured at planning and re-checked by you in step 1(f):

1. **REWORK IS NOT AN EXISTING ENTRY.** `BOARD_COLUMNS` (board-columns.ts:17-19) is exactly `PLANNED, WORKING, REVIEW, VERIFIED, LANDED, PUBLISHED`. `grep -rn "REWORK" apps/control-room/src` and `git grep -n "REWORK" -- apps/daemon/src` (tests excluded) both return ZERO.
2. **NOTHING MOVES A NODE ON REJECTION.** `preview-daemon-edge.ts:68-78` commits a `PreviewDecisionRecord` whose `findings` NAME nodes of the active graph (`:71`). It records a verdict; no node status changes.
3. **RAIL 2 FORBIDS THE OBVIOUS FIX**: "a new board column is a design regression, not a feature."

Raised to the governor at 14:46Z (msg-bc9b0f54) with three options: (A) narrow the clause to "the findings render against the named node, no column move" — my recommendation, since the daemon already records which nodes the findings name; (B) authorize a REWORK column, waiving rail 2; (C) file a second daemon leaf for the node-state transition and gate this row on it.

**WHAT TO DO:** record in the step note what you measured, and whether a ruling has landed on the row or in #architects. **If a ruling exists, follow it.** If not, `moe.report_blocked` naming this clause and citing msg-bc9b0f54 — the other six DoD items are done by then, so the row is one ruling from complete.

**DO NOT** invent a column, add one to `BOARD_COLUMNS`, assert against a column you created, or quietly skip the clause and claim the DoD met. The first three break rail 2; the last is a false completion claim.

**WHAT YOU CAN BUILD NOW REGARDLESS:** the Reject-with-findings CONTROL itself and the findings text rendering are reachable and are part of DoD 1's "both Approve and Reject-with-findings controls". Build the control, spend the offer, render the findings against the named node. Only the COLUMN ASSERTION is blocked.

amendments.description:
**DoD 3 — RULED. BUILD IT. The earlier "stop and report" is superseded.**

When I wrote this step, DoD 3 asked you to assert a node moved to a **REWORK** column, and that was unsatisfiable on two counts: `BOARD_COLUMNS` (board-columns.ts:17-19) is exactly six entries with no REWORK, and nothing in the daemon moves a node on rejection — `preview-daemon-edge.ts:68-78` commits a `PreviewDecisionRecord` whose `findings` NAME nodes of the active graph (`:71`) and changes no status. Meanwhile rail 2 forbids adding a column.

**The governor ruled option (A) at 14:49Z and has edited the DoD field.** DoD 3 now reads:

> "REJECT with findings renders the findings against the named node on the card and in the activity words; the node's board column does NOT change; `BOARD_COLUMNS` stays its six entries; assert the finding text on the rejected node, the existing path back to work, and an unchanged column read before and after."

**WHAT TO BUILD:**

1. **THE FINDINGS RENDER AGAINST THE NAMED NODE**, on the card and in the activity words. The daemon already tells you which node each finding names — `PreviewFinding` carries `nodeRef` and `detail` — so render the finding text against that node rather than as a loose blob. A rejection whose reason the operator cannot tie to a node is the defect the original clause was reaching for.

2. **THE COLUMN DOES NOT CHANGE, AND THAT IS ASSERTED, NOT ASSUMED.** Read the node's board column BEFORE the rejection and AFTER it, and assert they are equal. This is the arm that makes the ruling durable: it pins that the product does not silently grow a node transition later without someone noticing.

3. **`BOARD_COLUMNS` STAYS ITS SIX ENTRIES** — `PLANNED, WORKING, REVIEW, VERIFIED, LANDED, PUBLISHED`. Assert the roster length and membership so a future row cannot add a seventh without this arm reddening. **Do NOT add REWORK** (rail 2: "a new board column is a design regression, not a feature").

4. **THE EXISTING PATH BACK TO WORK IS SHOWN.** The operator has just rejected; the card must make the next action reachable through whatever path already exists, not through a new one invented here.

**WHAT NOT TO DO, unchanged from before:** do not add a column, do not invent a node transition, do not assert against a state you created. The daemon records which nodes the findings name — that is the actionable information, and rendering it is the whole of this clause now.

**The Reject-with-findings CONTROL itself** is part of DoD 1 and was already buildable; if you built it in step 3, this step adds the rendering and the two invariance arms on top.
amendments.reason: Governor 14:49Z ruled option (A) on DoD 3 and edited the DoD field: no REWORK column, no invented node transition, rail 2 stands. The step told you to STOP and check for a ruling — the ruling now exists, so this replaces the stop with the work. Build it; do not block.

implementationPlan.description:
DOCS, DRILLS, GATES, SELF-REVIEW.

**(a) DOCS (DoD 6), MINIMAL EDIT.** `README.md` collides with FIVE peer rows — change only the sentence the DoD names and rebase around their text. Rewrite the "no working preview" clause to the measured truth and confirm `git grep -n "no working preview"` returns 0. **If the live drive did not happen, say so plainly rather than implying it did** — DoD 6 asks for exactly that honesty.

**(b) LIVE DRIVE (DoD 6):** a preview started for UnAI or a fresh scaffold app, with a real screenshot (path + sha256) and the committed decision, in a row comment under ~4500 chars (comments truncate silently at 5000). If it did not happen, record that instead — never imply a drive you did not run.

**(c) DRILLS.** `git status --porcelain` every path you will mutate and RECORD it. For EVERY path — tracked or not — back it up out of tree (%TEMP%, suffixed with your worker id) and **restore FROM THE BACKUP, never `git checkout --`**: a tracked file can hold a peer's uncommitted delivery, and three rows are editing `needs-you-model.ts` concurrently. Prove each restore in a call SEPARATE from the restore — for a CLEAN path an empty `git diff` confirms it; **for a path already ` M`, sha256 against the backup is the ONLY admissible proof**, because there an empty `git diff` means you reverted the peer and the reassuring output is byte-identical to the catastrophic one.

THREE MUTATIONS, each alone, the named arm confirmed RED, then restored:
  1. Render the card when no receipt exists -> the DoD-1 absence arm reds.
  2. Assert the approve verdict from component state instead of `/activity/read` -> the DoD-2 arm should red when the click does not reach the daemon. **This drill proves the arm tests the daemon, not the DOM.**
  3. Swallow an unknown refusal code to blank -> the DoD-4 verbatim arm reds.

**(d) GATES**, each standalone and foreground: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`, `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test`, `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm test`, and `pnpm test:e2e:browser` with its SPEC COUNT quoted and the spec named. Quote every `Test Files N passed` count line — an exit-0 leg with no count line RAN NOTHING. Note which legs cover no `apps/**` file rather than offering a bare root count as evidence.

**(e) ADVERSARIAL PASS** — answer in writing: Can the card render from anything other than a real daemon receipt? Does Approve prove the daemon received it, or only that the DOM changed? Does an unknown code ever render blank? Does the aria-live region re-announce on every poll? Did any peer's `NEEDS_YOU_KINDS` entry get dropped in a rebase? Is any preview process or port left alive after the journey?

**(f)** DECLARE EVERY PATH in `complete_step.modifiedFiles`, then re-check `git status --porcelain` for anything unreported, including mutate-and-restore paths, which must show CLEAN.

STEP 1 PREREQUISITE VERIFICATION - FULL MEASUREMENT (the block reason is capped at 2000 chars; this is the evidence it points at). worker-0520a42e, 2026-09-06, HEAD eb13d2f6 on moe/work-2026-09-04.      if (preview) {
       const decoded = decodePreviewDecidePayload(envelope.payload);
       if (!decoded.ok) {
         throw new DomainRefusal(decoded.code, decoded.layer, "preview.decide payload refused");
       }
       const stub = previewRefusal("PREVIEW_GOAL_NOT_LANDED");

   EVERY well-formed decision - APPROVE and REJECT alike - throws PREVIEW_GOAL_NOT_LANDED @ GOAL_AUTHORITY. Only a MALFORMED payload gets a different code. Nothing is ever committed, so nothing can be read back from /activity/read.

2. THE RUNNER PACKAGE HAS ZERO CONSUMERS.
     git grep -n "preview/preview-" -- '*.ts' '*.tsx' '*.js' ':!*/dist/*' ':!apps/daemon/src/preview/*'

DoD REACHABILITY, clause by clause. 1: no receipt and no offer to render from. 2: the registry refuses every APPROVE - precisely the defect the clause exists to catch. 3: REJECT never commits, so no node moves to REWORK. 5: no start and no approve for Playwright to drive. 6: cannot drive UnAI. Clauses 4 (stage + refusal words) and 7 (gates) are the only reachable ones, and neither is worth landing alone.

AMENDMENT CHECK (global rail 9): all eight steps have activeAmendmentId=None and zero amendments, so the base plan text is authoritative and this block is premised on the effective text.

ACTIONS TAKEN: filed task-dd86f35e117e4de1b5b885332d8af1f8 (PLANNING, CRITICAL, dependsOn task-f5a74c23 + task-40e52fa8) for the registry edge, the start trigger, the affordance offer and the shutdown sweep; commented the consumer-edge measurement on task-f5a74c23 (global rail 4 clause 1 puts it on the producer's record, not a reopen); commented the band-shape finding on the parent task-f3edb8fb with the architect ask.

comments.content:
